hypotheses.claim: ConstTag/VariableDeclaration client transform wraps @const initializers in $.derived(() => ...) but never marks the callback async when the initializer contains await, so `{@const number = await Promise.resolve(5)}` emits `const number = $.derived(() => await ...)` which is a syntax error inside a non-async function.
evidence_refs: baseline compiled_client: `const number = $.derived(() => await Promise.resolve(5));` inside boundary pending/main blocks
hypotheses.prediction: Marking the derived callback async (and routing the const through the async-derived path so downstream reads await it) makes the holdout render '5' in client and hydrate modes.
hypotheses.falsifier: If the fix instead requires rewriting the await into a promise-chain/thunk (e.g. `$.async` body transforms) because async derived callbacks are not supported by the runtime, an async-callback-only patch will still fail or misrender.

hypotheses.claim: The bug is in analysis rather than transform: ConstTag analysis does not register the await containment, so the transform lacks the async flag/context and emits a sync derived, whereas template-level awaits (e.g. {#if} expressions) correctly detect `options.async` and use async derived callbacks.
evidence_refs: baseline compiled output showing sync derived callback despite await
IfBlock.js inspected 50-89 showing awaited expressions handled in block transforms
hypotheses.prediction: Adding await-containment tracking to ConstTag analysis (or passing `is_async` into the VariableDeclaration/ConstTag transform state) will produce `$.derived(async () => ...)` and the reproducer will pass.
hypotheses.falsifier: If VariableDeclaration already handles async callbacks when a flag is set but the flag is never set for const tags, an analysis-only fix changes nothing in output; conversely if the transform hardcodes sync derived regardless of flags, analysis changes also fail.
